paper_metadata.title: Effects of annealing temperature on the microstructure, textures and tensile properties of cold-rolled Fe–13Cr–4Al alloys with different Nb contents

evidence.quote: four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloys with different Nb contents (0 – 1.5 wt%) were prepared by using vacuum induction melting, forging, hot rolling, and cold rolling.
Four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloys with different Nb contents were fabricated, denoted as 0Nb, 0.5Nb, 1Nb and 1.5Nb.
Four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloys with different Nb contents were fabricated, denoted as 0Nb, 0.5Nb, 1Nb and 1.5Nb.
Four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloys with different Nb contents were fabricated, denoted as 0Nb, 0.5Nb, 1Nb and 1.5Nb.
Four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloys with different Nb contents were fabricated, denoted as 0Nb, 0.5Nb, 1Nb and 1.5Nb.
Four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloy ingots were made by vacuum induction melting with pure raw materials.
Then the four ingots were homogenized at 1100 ◦C for 3 h and followed by hot-forging into sheets with thickness of ~10 mm.
Then the four ingots were homogenized at 1100 ◦C for 3 h and followed by hot-forging into sheets with thickness of ~10 mm.
The as-forged sheets were hot-rolled at 800 ◦C with a ~70% thickness reduction through 6 passes. The supplementary heating temperature between each pass was 800 ◦C, and the time was 5 min.
After that the hot-rolled plates were cold-rolled with a total ~50% thickness reduction. The final thickness of all the plates is ~1.5 mm.
Then the as-rolled plates were sectioned into small samples by electrical discharge machining (EDM).
These small samples were annealed with different temperatures ranging from 600 ◦C – 1100 ◦C with an interval of 50 ◦C for 30 min followed by air cooling.

evidence.section: 3.2 Precipitates in the deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: The cold-rolled 1Nb sheet also precipitated many small second phase particles (marked by red arrows) in Fig. 11 (a), with a size of ~100 nm.

evidence.section: 3.2 Precipitates in the deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: Additionally, the size of the second phase particles (as indicated by the red arrows) in Fig. 12 (a) was also dramatically increased to ~ 500 nm.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: For all the specimens, elongated grains were observed along the RD, and many fine subgrains were also observed within the elongated grains.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: The subgrains within the deformed grains were gradually refined from 10.5 μm to 2.3 μm and the number of subgrains increased in proportion to the Nb content.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: the 0Nb microstructure annealed at 700 ◦C consisted of equiaxed grains with an average size of 5.4 μm, indicating that full recrystallization occurred at this temperature.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: The deformed band structure was gradually refined with the increase of Nb content.

Because of the effects of solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening and fine grain strengthening produced by the addition of Nb element, the strength and hardness of the alloys increased with the increase of Nb content.

evidence.section: 3.2 Precipitates in the deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: a small number of Laves phase particles were found in the as-rolled 0.5Nb sheet, with a size of ~0.2 μm, which precipitated during the preliminary treatment.

evidence.section: 3.2 Precipitates in the deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: The cold-rolled 1Nb sheet also precipitated many small second phase particles (marked by red arrows) in Fig. 11 (a), with a size of ~100 nm.

evidence.section: 3.2 Precipitates in the deformed and annealed samples
evidence.quote: Additionally, the size of the second phase particles (as indicated by the red arrows) in Fig. 12 (a) was also dramatically increased to ~ 500 nm. The same thickness stripes were also clearly observed, as shown by the blue arrows, indicating that well-indexed grain boundaries formed in this area. The second phase particles mainly distributed at grain boundaries.

Because of the effects of solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening and fine grain strengthening produced by the addition of Nb element, the strength and hardness of the alloys increased with the increase of Nb content.
